articles.headline: Enterprise among our Colored Men
articles.summary: We take great pleasure in noticing the fact, that our men of color are beginning to realize the fact that more men of business are needed among them. Several have already shown that they understand this. We will not now particularize, but shall do so in an early number.

articles.headline: A Correction
articles.summary: In our last issue, in the marriage by Rev. J. H. Lowber [VERIFY initials], the lady's name should have been inserted Mrs. Eliza Hazzard, of New London, Penn. Bro. Lowber threw us completely off the track, and caused us to neglect congratulating the happy couple, which we now do.

articles.headline: The Excursion to Atlantic City
articles.summary: In another column will be found an advertisement of an excursion from our friends to Atlantic city. It promises to be one of the most recherche of the season. The price of tickets is $1.25, which answers going and returning. From the names of those having the matter in charge, we anticipate it will be a success. Mr. Bryant, the well known manager of the road, will spare no pains to provide for the comfort of all who may desire to attend.

articles.headline: For the Sea Shore. A Grand Excursion and Pic-nic to Atlantic City (For Colored Persons Exclusively)
articles.summary: Will take place on Tuesday, Sept. 5, 1865. Fare going and returning, $1.25. Children under 10 years of age, 65 cts. Tickets for sale at the Railroad Office, at the wharf, two hours before starting. Last Boat leaves Vine St. Ferry at 6.30 A. M. Committee of Arrangements.

articles.headline: Bethel A. M. E. Sabbath School
articles.summary: This, the oldest, and probably the largest and best Sabbath school belonging to the A. M. E. Church in America, celebrated last Wednesday, 30th inst., by an excursion to Diamond Cottage. The morning was everything else except a favorable one, but as old Sol began to shine forth and the lowering clouds to disperse, the hearts of thousands were made glad, in anticipation of a merry time.

articles.headline: Home for Disabled Colored Soldiers. An Appeal
articles.author: Anne de B. Mears
articles.summary: We take peculiar pleasure in calling attention to the letter published below, which has been sent us by a lady well known to many of our brave soldiers, who have experienced the benefits of her kind consideration while in the hospital at Camp William Penn. To the Editor of the Christian Recorder: Sir: Through the columns of your widely-circulated paper among the colored population of Philadelphia and elsewhere, I wish to make an appeal in behalf of the disabled colored soldiers who have been discharged from the service, many of them have no homes or any one to care for them.

articles.headline: Wanted (workmen on tin and sheet-iron)
articles.author: Wm. Still
articles.summary: The subscriber is in want of several good workmen on tin and sheet-iron in his stove store. Freedmen or others deprived of following their trades, owing to the controlling prejudices of white mechanics, would do well to apply immediately, as the highest wages will be paid. Besides this, to such as may prove capable and steady, a rare chance is offered for advancement in a business aspect. Wm. Still, Stove Warehouse, 107 North Fifth Street, Philadelphia. (Sept. 9, 3t.)

articles.headline: Letter from Texas (29th Connecticut Volunteers)
articles.author: Charles W. Cole
articles.summary: 29th Reg't. Conn. Vols., Brownsville, Texas, August, 20th, 1865. Mr. Editor: Sir, I have for a long time been a steady peruser of your valuable paper, and have found much therein to cultivate a good mind. It was sent to me by a friend in Philadelphia, during most of the time that I spent in Virginia, in the campaign of 1864. As there are few in our ranks from Philadelphia and none of them seem inclined to do so, I take the liberty to pen you a few lines.

articles.headline: Shameful
articles.summary: A few days ago, a very distinguished lady of our acquaintance, and another from Baltimore, got into one of the Spruce and Pine Street cars. Upon collecting the fare, the conductor discovered that they were colored persons. They were ordered to quit the car, but declined doing so. The car was then driven off at a furious rate.

articles.headline: The Institute for Colored Youth

Miss Mapps has been a faithful laborer in the cause of education. Miss Fanny Jackson, one of Oberlin's best graduates, has taken Miss Mapp's place. We know of no one who is better fitted to fill the vacancy in every way than Miss Fanny Jackson, in a moral, religious, and literary capacity.

events.name: Pennsylvania State Equal Rights' League, annual meeting at Harrisburg: afternoon and evening sessions of August 9
events.location: Harrisburg, Pennsylvania
events.description: Continuation of the proceedings (the first part ran the week before). Afternoon session, 2 1/2 o'clock, President Peck in the chair. Rules of order reported by the Committee on Rules (James McC. Crummill of Philadelphia, chairman; O. L. C. Hughes; Nath'l. W. Depee): three sessions daily, the evening one public; one-third of enrolled members a quorum; Matthias's Manual to govern. Solicitor Bustill paid in forty dollars from auxiliaries No. 14, Altoona E. R. League ($15, representatives Wm. Nesbit and John Alexander), No. 15, Hollidaysburg E. R. League ($15, Dan'l. Williams and Moses Brown) and No. 16, Huntingdon E. R. League ($10, John G. Chaplin). Committee on Credentials (Joseph C. Bustill, chairman; Daniel Williams; Aaron L. Still; E. R. Parker; C. H. Kelley [VERIFY]) certified these representatives: Henderson Davis, Jr., Lincoln E. R. League, 1st District of Philadelphia; Lorenzo D. Blackston [VERIFY], Rising Sun E. R. League, 2d District of Philadelphia; Chas. W. Nighten [VERIFY], New Castle E. R. League, Lawrence Co.; Henry T. Burley, Benevolent E. R. League, Erie; Franklin Johnson, Bellefonte E. R. League, Centre Co.; William Nesbit and John Alexander, Altoona; Daniel Williams and Moses Brown, Hollidaysburg; John G. Chaplin, Huntingdon. Henry T. Burley of Erie made Assistant Secretary pro tem. On motion of J. C. White, Jr., of Philadelphia, a Business Committee was named: Prof. G. B. Vashon of Pittsburg, chairman; O. L. C. Hughes of Harrisburg; B. Pulpress of Allegheny City; William D. Forten of Philadelphia; Rev. James Henry of Birmingham; later enlarged, on motion of Mr. Bustill, by Jas. McC. Crummill of Philadelphia, C. W. Nighten of New Castle, John Alexander of Altoona and Aaron L. Still of Reading. Finance Committee: Nath'l. W. Depee of Philadelphia, chairman; Edward R. Parker of Allegheny City; Samuel Molson [VERIFY] of Lewistown; George W. Dimey of Allegheny City; Rev. C. J. Carter of Harrisburg. Mr. Bustill of Philadelphia offered resolutions on the circulation of petitions and invited the choirs of the city to furnish music at the evening meetings; Mr. Fauset [VERIFY] of Philadelphia offered a resolution on the collection of statistics, and later one on the taxation of auxiliary leagues by membership. The Business Committee's report urged leagues in every county, town, village and hamlet, spoke of colored people 'taunted, insulted and cowardly assaulted on the highways by ruffians, on rail-roads by conductors, and driven from hotels and places of amusement', and offered a petition to Congress for a constitutional amendment forbidding legislation against any civilized portion of the inhabitants on account of race or color, with resolutions to petition the Pennsylvania Legislature, to send blank petitions to every League, Church and Lodge, and to appoint canvassers to gather statistics of the numbers, wealth and occupation of the colored people of the State. Finance Committee (N. W. Depee) recommended a one dollar tax; at the evening session (8 o'clock, President Peck in the chair) this was amended on motion of J. C. White, Jr., to tax every member of the League one dollar. Article 10th of the State League constitution was struck out and Article 12th amended, on Mr. Bustill's motions, to let auxiliaries connect directly with the National Equal Rights' League. An amendment by Prof. G. B. Vashon giving extra votes for cash paid in was voted down. Solicitor Bustill reported No. 17, Pittsburg E. R. League (Prof. Geo. B. Vashon, representative), with its ten dollar fee. The choirs of the city sang 'My Country, 'tis of thee'. The meeting went into committee of the whole on the state of the League, Mr. J. C. Bustill of Philadelphia in the chair, and adjourned to 10 o'clock the next morning.
attendees: chairman, Committee on Rules; added to the Business Committee; of Philadelphia (Dr.)
Committee on Rules; chairman, Finance Committee; of Philadelphia
Solicitor; chairman, Committee on Credentials; chairman of the committee of the whole; of Philadelphia
representative, Lincoln E. R. League, 1st District of Philadelphia
of Philadelphia; moved the Business Committee and the one dollar tax (printed 'J. C. White, Jr.')

events.name: Hop at the Banneker House, Cape Island, broken up by the proprietress
events.location: Banneker House, Cape Island (Cape May), New Jersey
events.description: A grand hop for the guests of the Banneker House was arranged for the evening of the 17th by Messrs. R. H. Gleaves, Chas. B. Colly [VERIFY], David R. Chester, John C. Bowers and Thomas Charnock, of Philadelphia, Dr. Hudson and Mr. Tennant, of Baltimore, and others. The party assembled at half past 9 o'clock. At fifteen minutes past twelve, as the last quadrille was being made up, the proprietress or her son had the gas turned out in both parlors, and then demanded ten dollars for the use of the parlors and injury to the matting, which the committee paid. The writer (signed with a pen name not clearly legible) reports that Mrs. Teagle called the company 'nothing but hotel boys and gamblers', and protests that proprietors are public servants and not judges of who are fit associates for their guests.

events.name: Grand Excursion and Pic-nic to Atlantic City (for colored persons exclusively)
events.location: Atlantic City, N. J.; last boat from Vine St. Ferry, Philadelphia, 6.30 A. M.
events.description: Advertised excursion and pic-nic 'For Colored Persons Exclusively' on Tuesday, Sept. 5, 1865. Fare going and returning $1.25, children under 10 years 65 cts.; tickets at the Railroad Office at the wharf two hours before starting. Committee of Arrangements: James W. Purnell, Thos. H. Dorsey, Henry Jones, Joshua Brown, A. M. Reilly, A. Bernard; O. Davis, Sec. The editor's notice on page 2 calls it probably the last opportunity of the season and names Mr. Bryant as manager of the road.

events.name: Bethel A. M. E. Sabbath School excursion to Diamond Cottage
events.location: Diamond Cottage (reached by boat from Philadelphia)
events.description: Annual excursion of the Bethel A. M. E. Sabbath School on Wednesday, the 30th (August 30, 1865). The crowd that followed the school was large; 'it is estimated by some that over seven thousand were present at one time', and the boats were crowded during the whole day. Everything passed off pleasantly 'with one or two exceptions'. Clergy present: Revs. Wm. Moore, Cuff, Turpin, Cornish, Smith, Stevenson, Atwell and others. The teachers and the superintendent (not named) are credited with keeping order. The editor left at 8 P. M.

events.name: District Grand Lodge, No. 2, Independent Order of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria: quarterly meeting
events.location: Philadelphia Institute Hall, Lombard street, above 7th, Philadelphia
events.description: Quarterly meeting of the Grand Lodge called for Tuesday, September 5th, at 10 o'clock A. M.; officers, members and the representatives of the several lodges under its jurisdiction notified to attend. By order of the R. W. G. Chief (not named); Wm. A. Smith, R. W. G. R. Sec'y. The same column carries the call of the Right Worthy National Grand Council of the order for a Grand Convocation at Georgetown, D. C., on Tuesday, September 19th, 1865 (John H. Anthony, R. W. N. G. Chief, and Wm. H. Wood, R. W. N. G. Sec., both of Baltimore).

events.name: Brick Wesley Sabbath School annual excursion
events.location: Philadelphia (destination not stated)
events.description: Notice dated Sept. 2 that the Brick Wesley Sabbath School will make its annual excursion on Thursday, September 14th. No officers or destination are named.

events.name: National Equal Rights League: first annual session called
events.location: Cleveland, Ohio
events.description: Call dated from the Bureau of the National Equal Rights League, Philadelphia, August 14, 1865, for the first annual session of the League on the first Tuesday of September, 1865, at 10 o'clock A. M., in Cleveland, O. The call says that the question of 'our right to full citizenship' is not yet defined and has only been removed to the forum. By order of the President, John M. Langston; St. George R. Taylor, Secretary.

events.name: Celebration of several benevolent societies at Langhorn's Hill, near Attleborough
events.location: Langhorn's Hill, near Attleborough, Bucks county, Pa.
events.description: Celebration of several benevolent societies (not named), with an invitation to 'all like institutions and a generous public'; dinner on the ground at 50 cents and feed for horses. By order of the committee: Thomas Gouwens [VERIFY surname], Pres.; John Newman, Sec. Notice first inserted Aug. 19.

events.name: Appeal for a Home for Disabled Colored Soldiers (Camp William Penn hospital)
events.location: Philadelphia; donations to the Milestown P. O., 22d Ward, or Col. R. R. Corson, 133 Walnut St.
events.description: Letter dated Philadelphia, Aug. 9th, 1865, from Anne de B. Mears, who knew many of the wounded men at the hospital at Camp William Penn, asking that ten thousand dollars ($10,000) be subscribed as a beginning toward a home for disabled colored soldiers discharged from the service, to be continued after their lifetime as an institution for aged colored men. She asks 'the colored men' to be the first to contribute. Donations to her address through the Milestown P. O., 22d Ward, or left with Col. R. R. Corson, 133 Walnut St., Philadelphia; all donations to be acknowledged through the papers. The editor endorses the plan and says it 'is directed by those who are tried friends of our people'.

events.name: Funeral sermon of Rev. Robert Evans at Bethel A. M. E. Church, Burlington
events.location: Bethel A. M. E. Church, Burlington, N. J.
events.description: Funeral sermon of Rev. Robert Evans to be delivered on the third Sabbath in September (17th inst.) at 10 1/2 o'clock A. M. by Rev. Joshua Woodlin, of Brooklyn, N. Y. Notice signed T. Gould, Pastor.
attendees: pastor, Bethel A. M. E. Church, Burlington

events.name: Horntown Sunday School annual excursion (Chester Circuit)
events.location: Ashar's Woods [VERIFY spelling], just below the church, Horntown (Chester Circuit, Pa.)
events.description: The Horntown Sunday School's annual excursion on Thursday, September 14th, with addresses by several ministers and speaking by the children. Signed Peter Gardiner, Minister in Charge. The same issue gives his quarterly meetings: Horntown, Sept. 16th at 2 1/2 o'clock; Chester on the 24th; Chichester, October 1st.

events.name: Excursion for Colored People Only, Philadelphia to Atlantic City
events.location: Vine Street wharf, Philadelphia, to Atlantic City, N. J.
events.description: A second 'colored people only' railroad excursion (after that of Sept. 5), Tuesday, September 12th, 1865: leaves Vine Street wharf 6.30 A. M., Cooper's Point 6.51, Haddonfield 7.12, Ashland 7.18, White Horse 7.24, Longacoming 7.37; arrives Atlantic City 9.48 A. M.; returns 5.18 P. M. Round trip $1.25 from Vine St. wharf and Cooper's Point, $1 from Haddonfield, Ashland, White Horse and Longacoming. Tickets at the wharf and Cooper's Point on the morning, on the cars, of the station agents, and 'of the subscribers in Haddonfield'. Signed B. Coffin (not known to be Black; entered as printed, not linked).

events.name: Magic lantern exhibition at John Wesley M. E. Church
events.location: John Wesley M. E. Church, Shippen Street, above Seventh, Philadelphia
events.description: George Thornton, from Winchester, Va., to exhibit his magic lanterns, with scriptural subjects, on Monday and Tuesday, September 11th and 12th, at 8 o'clock P. M.

events.name: Assembly of delegates of the colored Masonic Grand Lodges (A. Y. M.) at Philadelphia
events.location: Philadelphia (place of meeting not stated)
events.description: Notice dated A. L. 5865, Philadelphia, September 11th, 1865, from the Grand Lodge for the State of Pennsylvania, A. Y. M.: delegates from the several Grand Lodges to assemble in Philadelphia on Tuesday, October 10th [VERIFY day: the numeral is soft; Oct. 10, 1865 was a Tuesday], at 10 o'clock A. M., 'to protect Masonry from being mixed up with modern innovation' and to 'inculcate a spirit of peace and unity among the craft'. Grand Lodges to be represented: Most Worthy United Grand Lodge of New York (Patrick H. Reason, G. M.); M. W. Grand Lodge of the State of Pennsylvania (Jonathan Miller, G. M.); M. W. Union Grand Lodge of Jersey (Moses Wilcox, G. M.); M. W. Hiram Grand Lodge of Delaware (John W. Layton, G. M.); M. W. First Independent Grand Lodge of Maryland (Lemuel G. Griffin, G. M.). Committee of Arrangements: New York, J. H. Townsend, Ransom F. Wake, George Lawrence, Jr., Wm. R. Connor, Wm. C. H. Curtis; Pennsylvania, Jacob Jenkins [VERIFY], John Rhodes, Thomas Fauset, Edward Young. To run Sept. 16 to Oct. 7.

events.name: Zion A. M. E. Mission Church: second quarterly meeting
events.location: Zion A. M. E. Mission Church, Seventh street, between Dickerson and Tasker streets, Philadelphia
events.description: Second quarterly meeting on Sunday, September 24th, with 'several strange ministers' expected to preach. H. J. Rhodes, Pastor in charge.

events.name: John Wesley M. E. church: quarterly meeting
events.location: John Wesley M. E. church, Shippen street, above Seventh, Philadelphia
events.description: Quarterly meeting on Sabbath, September 17th, 1865: preaching at half-past ten by Rev. Robert Robertson, at three by Rev. John G. Manluff, Presiding Elder, and at eight by Rev. A. Brown. Notice dated Philada., Sep. 13, 1865.

events.name: Union Camp-meeting in Asher Borden's woods, near Allentown, N. J.
events.location: Asher Borden's woods, half a mile from Allentown, Monmouth county, N. J.
events.description: Union camp-meeting from Wednesday, September 20th, to the 27th. Committee of Arrangement, all members of the A. M. E. Church: Saml. H. Smith, Isaiah Dillon, Gilbert Woodby [VERIFY], Saml. Reason [VERIFY]. Speakers: Rev. Anthony L. Stanford at 3 o'clock P. M.; Rev. Thomas H. Cooper at 7 o'clock; Rev. Joseph Long at ten o'clock A. M. Persons from Philadelphia leave Walnut street wharf at nine o'clock A. M. and two o'clock P. M. for Bordentown, then by stage to Allentown. Signed Rev. George Waters and Rev. Saml. H. Smith, Ministers of the Gospel; Rev. Jos. C. Miller, Proprietor. Dated Philada., Sept. 12, '65.

events.name: African United Temperance Beneficial Society of Bordentown: resolutions on the death of Rev. Robert Evans
events.location: Bordentown, N. J.
events.description: Meeting of the African United Temperance Beneficial Society (A. U. T. B. Society) of Bordentown, N. J., which passed resolutions on the death of Rev. Robert Evans, who 'departed this life in Philadelphia, July 5, '65', 'our founder, and who for a number of years presided over our deliberations', and condoled with his family. Committee: Rev. Abraham C. Griffin, Gideon Lewis, Hudson Wood. Dated Bordentown, N. J., Aug. 25, '65. (His funeral sermon at Burlington was set for Sept. 17: see CR_1865-09-09.)

events.name: Two colored ladies carried off and insulted on a Spruce and Pine Street car
events.location: Spruce and Pine Street passenger railway, Philadelphia
events.description: STREETCAR exclusion. 'A few days ago' (before Sept. 23, 1865) 'a very distinguished lady of our acquaintance, and another from Baltimore' (neither named) got into one of the Spruce and Pine Street cars. When the conductor, collecting the fare, found they were colored, they were ordered to quit the car and declined. The car was then driven off at a furious rate; when they asked to get out they were not allowed, 'but told that they should be taken out to the depot and be whitewashed'. One of them jumped from the car at the risk of her life. During the trip they were made to endure 'the most insulting language'. The editor adds: 'The conductor and the number of his car are known.'

events.name: Institute for Colored Youth: Grace A. Mapps resigns; Fanny Jackson and Mary Patterson appointed
events.location: Institute for Colored Youth, Philadelphia
events.description: Reported Sept. 23, 1865: Miss Grace A. Mapps, a teacher in the school for some twelve years, has resigned as Principal of the Girls' department. Miss Fanny Jackson, 'one of Oberlin's best graduates', has taken her place, subject to the approbation of the Board of Directors; the editor believes it is her first visit to Philadelphia. Her assistant is Miss Mary Patterson, also a graduate of Oberlin College, 'from our own State, North Carolina'. Elsewhere on the page Mr. E. D. Bassett is named as 'Principal of our Colored High School' who spoke before the American Institute of Instruction at New Haven, Conn.
attendees: retiring Principal of the Girls' department
new Principal of the Girls' department
Principal (printed 'Mr. E. D. Bassett, Principal of our Colored High School')

events.name: Bethel church missionary prayer-meeting: organization to be completed
events.location: Basement of Bethel A. M. E. Church, Philadelphia
events.description: Bethel church has organized a missionary prayer-meeting; its organization is to be completed 'on next Tuesday night' (Sept. 26, 1865) in the basement of the church. No officers named.

events.name: Ladies' Union Association: donation from its Zoar church auxiliary
events.location: Philadelphia
events.description: The Ladies' Union Association (A. E. Mills, President) acknowledges $14.67 received from its Auxiliary at Zoar church (printed 'Zoar A. M. E. Church'; Zoar was the M. E. church in the Northern Liberties), Mrs. Isaiah Ware [VERIFY: Ware or Wears], President of the auxiliary.

events.name: Funeral discourse by Rev. Elisha Weaver at Wesley church
events.location: Wesley church, Hurst street, Philadelphia
events.description: Rev. Elisha Weaver, editor of the Christian Recorder, to preach a funeral discourse at Wesley church, Hurst street, 'on next Sabbath' (Sept. 24, 1865) at 10 1/2 o'clock. The person commemorated is not named. Signed J. Mitchell, Pastor.

events.name: Farewell sermon of Rev. James Hamilton at the Union Baptist Church
events.location: Union Baptist Church, Minster street, Philadelphia
events.description: Rev. James Hamilton, appointed to the charge of the African Baptist Church in Charleston, South Carolina, to deliver his farewell sermon on Sabbath evening, the 24th inst.; a collection to be taken up for the work of evangelizing the South.

notes: CR_1865-09-02 (Vol. V, No. 35, whole No. 244). Page 1: Albany letter of Wm. W. Grimes (Israel A. M. E. Church trustees and sewing circle, Albany names in text only, not entered); Equal Rights League proceedings; chapter XXVIII of 'The Curse of Caste; or the Slave Bride' by Mrs. Julia C. Collins; the Banneker House letter.

CR_1865-09-02 p2: 'Editorial Correspondence' is Weaver's Chicago and Springfield, Ill. journal (John Jones of Chicago etc.), out of scope. Raleigh correspondence describes the Fourth of July procession of the colored people of Raleigh, N. C. (Army band lent by General Ames, over five hundred flags, guard provided, no disturbance): out of town, not entered as an event.

CR_1865-09-02 p3: obituary of Harriet Myers, wife of Stephen Myers, Albany (signed W. H. J.), and Cincinnati and Baltimore death notices are out of town. Repeating ads seen and not re-entered: Mrs. H. T. O'Donnell (card, formerly of 740 South St., Lombard St. boarding house), S. Shorter Hawkins (615 Lombard), J. J. Lyons (1023 Lombard), T. J. Bowers coal (Lombard St.), R. H. Gleaves private boarding (633 Pine), Mrs. Maria Highgates (1026 Barley), Olive Branch (814 Lombard, Mrs. H. M. Cropper), Mrs. M. Bennett, the Bustills (403 S. Sixth), Nathaniel L. Durham (911 1/2 Christian), James C. Clark M. D., Mrs. Ann E. Foster (1733 Addison). White or out-of-town ads noted only: Wilson's map-mounting (31 South Sixth St., I. Wilson), Hudson's City Hotel (Baltimore), Hopkins' hoop skirts, Costar, Perry & Co., Jones' clothing, Matlack, Reimer, Pennsylvania Central Railroad, St. Charles United States Hotel (Raleigh), Vassar Female College, Wm. P. Powell (New York), Dandridge Kelly (Baltimore), Winston & Thomas (New Orleans).

CR_1865-09-02 p4: columns 1-4 are poetry, 'The Family', 'Child's Cabinet', 'Literary' and 'Science and Art' reprints. Ads in columns 5-7 are repeats (Globe Hotel and Wm. P. Powell, New York; Henderson's Capitol Clothing House, 510 Market; John H. Stokes; Charles Magarge; African Civilization Society; Book Depository catalogue; Mrs. M. C. Gibbons's intelligence office, 1113 Pine; Wm. H. Longfellow; Jane Johnson and Ann Wear, shrouding, 618 South Eighth; Mrs. H. S. Duterte; F. Champion; Thomas Charnock; Mrs. C. E. Harding, 713 Lombard; Avery College; James W. Brown steam-dyeing; Charles W. Brister; boarding at Fairhaven, N. J.; Jas. B. Rodgers, printer). The Lincoln Monument ad is dated 'jy 15 6m' and the Cape Island ads date from June, so they also ran in the July and August issues.

Scan quality: the film image is a soft bitonal scan; letters a/e/o and u/n are often indistinguishable even at higher DPI, so higher-resolution rechecks did not settle doubtful spellings. Doubtful names are flagged and not linked.

CR_1865-09-09 p2, Letter from Texas: Sergt. Charles W. Cole, Co. D, 29th Connecticut Vols., a Philadelphian ('long for the hour to come when I can return to the City of Brotherly Love'), writes: 'I see that the car fever rages as violently as ever with you, and I am sorry to see that Philadelphia is so far behind the times; but there will be a change when the regiments belonging there return'. A STREETCAR topic mention; no meeting or incident is named, so no event entered.

CR_1865-09-09 p2, Missouri Conference at Springfield, Ill. (Bishop Campbell presiding, Bishop Quinn assisting; bare 'Bishop Campbell' and 'Bishop Quinn' not linked): trial of Rev. A. T. Wood, the call on Governor Oglesby with John Jones and Lewis White of Chicago, and a visit to the burial vault of President Lincoln. Out of town; article only.

CR_1865-09-09 p3, Adger gift: the Charleston committee signing is Samuel Robertson, W. R. Spencer, Samuel Dawlins [reading uncertain], Jas. Bright, Alfred S. Owens, Thomas Savage [uncertain], H. R. Hamilton: Charleston men, text only.

CR_1865-09-09 (Vol. V, No. 36, whole No. 245). Page 1, read in full: poem 'My Mother' (M.); 'Letters from Richmond, No. 1' (S. M. O.); 'Phrenology No. 10' by J. Anderson Raymond; letter from Rev. James Lynch on Georgia (Richmond, Aug. 30); 'Exhibition and Examination' in Louisville (A. B.); letter from Chester, Ills. (J. M. Wilkinson); army correspondence from Fort Butler, Donaldsonville, La. (William P. Green, Co. F, 11th U. S. C. Heavy Artillery, on punishments, the 'sweat box'); 'The Curse of Caste' chapter XXIX. No Philadelphia names on the page.

CR_1865-09-09 p2 other contents: editorial 'Reconstruction: the Duty of the Oppressed'; 'The Wonderful Works of Nature. Astronomy' (John Henry L. Huston); letter from Rev. G. A. Rue, Newbern (colored convention at Raleigh called for Sept. 29); 'Commendable' (soldiers' religious association at Boca Chica, Texas, 21 signers, regiment not stated); letter from Vicksburg (Sarah Woodson); 'General Morgan versus Colored Soldiers' (signed 'A Colored Soldier', Delaware, Ohio). Out of scope.

CR_1865-09-09 p3: letters from Natchez (Nelson Fitzhugh) and Delaware, O. (T. W. Roberts; 'Decorum'), Louisville obituary of Nancy Craig, death of Rev. George McMullin [spelling uncertain] at Trenton, N. J., Aug. 20, in his 76th year: text only. The Good Samaritans' Georgetown convocation call, the Brick Wesley excursion notice and the 'book that will be read' ad repeat from Sept. 2. Columns 4-7 are the same standing ads as Sept. 2 (Lincoln Monument, O'Donnell card, Hawkins, Lyons, Bowers at No. 634 Lombard, R. H. Gleaves, Highgates, Olive Branch, Bennett, Bustill, Durham, Clark, Foster): not re-entered.

CR_1865-09-09 p4: columns 1-4 poetry ('The Border Land'), 'Going to Church', 'A Sabbath Day's Journey', 'The Present Fashions', 'The Five Little Rabbits', 'Cures', 'Mosquitoes'. Columns 5-7 the standing ads as on Sept. 2 p4; the Banneker House (Mrs. Teagle) ad has dropped out; Mrs. H. C. Lunn's remains. No new ad.

CR_1865-09-16 (No. 37): only pages 3 and 4 survive (first sheet missing). Page 3 columns 1-3 viewed in full; the top of column 1 (end of a letter from a soldier or chaplain protesting harsh camp discipline) is too faint to read and its signer is on the lost sheet side. Column 2 top: 'Proverbs among the Freedmen', signed Jonathan C. Gibbs (from the South; mentions Bros. Adams, Randolph, Cardozo and Cain): article not entered beyond this note. Reprints: 'A Man Given as Food to the Dogs' (New Orleans Tribune), 'Can They Take Care of Themselves?'. Letter of James Lynch on the revival at Third Street A. M. E. church, Richmond (Sep. 9).

CR_1865-09-16 p3: Reading Equal Rights League tribute signed by its president (surname reads 'Underhill', initial unclear) and Henry B. Fry [reading uncertain], Sec'y: Reading men, text only. George G. Collins, 'a graduate of Oberlin College', appointed agent of the Recorder for Kentucky. Wm. Still's 'Wanted' (tin and sheet-iron workmen), the Chester Circuit notice (Peter Gardiner), the Good Samaritans' Georgetown call and the Delaware, Ohio camp-meeting notice (Turner W. Roberts) repeat or are out of town.

CR_1865-09-16 p3 columns 4-7 and p4: standing ads as on Sept. 2 and 9, nothing new; a Sterling's Ambrosia puff added. p4 columns 1-4: poem 'The Weeping Willow', 'Make the Most of Yourself', 'Twin Children in an Overflowed Basement' (a Philadelphia flood story from the Press naming Mrs. Sarah Johnson; no race given, not entered), 'Apologizing' by Gail Hamilton, natural history and science reprints.

'Rev. Robert Robertson' preaching at John Wesley M. E. church (Sept. 17, 1865) is recorded as printed; he is not the Rev. Richard Robinson of Frankford (died 1862). The officiating 'Rev. R. P. Gibbs' appears in both the Sept. 9 and Sept. 16 marriage columns with the same initials.

CR_1865-09-23 (Vol. V, No. 38, whole No. 247). Page 1 viewed in full: 'A Hymn of Trust'; letter from Paris (M. M. J. Brown); memorial of the Indiana Conference to Congress; 'Interesting Letter from Chicago' by 'Ruth' (Aug. 29): county convention of Aug. 21 on the franchise with John Jones, H. O. Wagoner, L. B. White; a resolution against colored barbers who will not shave colored men, a barber having refused to shave Rev. E. Weaver; Susan B. Anthony's lecture at Quinn's Chapel; letter from Delaware, Ohio ('Hannibal'); 'Zion Church Property Sacrificed' (Cincinnati); 'The Fifty-Fourth Massachusetts' (from the Tribune); 'The Curse of Caste' chapter XXXI. No Philadelphia names.

CR_1865-09-23 p2: Weaver's 'Editorial Correspondence' (Indianapolis, Richmond, Ind., Cincinnati, home on the 13th inst.); 'Colonel Frank Robertson' (St. Louis); 'Bishop Campbell in the West'; 'The Bench of Bishops and their Counsel'; 'Rev. Alexander Crummell's Speech' (which names E. D. Bassett); J. B. Smith's Lincoln Monument letter with a Newport, R. I. donor list (out of town); Bishop A. W. Wayman's letter on preaching at the Camden, Delaware camp meeting on Aug. 3 under threat of a mob (mentions a white Philadelphia Conference tract agent, name unclear); letter from Rev. Benjamin Lynch, New Brunswick, N. J. (Samuel G. Gould, President of the Equal Rights League of New Jersey, lectured; an auxiliary formed); Wm. L. Miller, Sergt. Major 22d U. S. C. T., Brownsville, Texas, answering M. R. Williams of the 41st U. S. C. T. on treatment of colored soldiers in Texas; letters from Charleston (Samuel Beaut [reading uncertain]) and Beaufort (J. W. Wright, naming Miss Mary Still and Miss Jennie Lynch as teachers among the freedmen). The Sept. 9 page 2 'Wanted' by Wm. Still is followed here by a puff naming 'Mr. Bowers' (T. J. Bowers, Lombard St.) too.

CR_1865-09-23 p3: Evangelical convention circular (Cleveland) delegate list, letter from Brownsville, Texas (Henry Augustine Hoy [reading uncertain], 43d? regiment, 25th Army Corps), D. P. Seaton's letter from Wilmington, Del., Western Theological Seminary (J. H. Turpin), Crummell's speech: not entered. Masonic notice, Still's 'Wanted' and the McDowell information-wanted repeat from Sept. 16. The Lincoln Monument ad has dropped out; new ads: Dr. J. W. Creek's 'Indian Rejuvenator' (Baltimore), Georgina Gleaves's trimmings ad (reset, dated Oct. [sic] 6m; her earlier ad was captured in Run #92, this is a new wording) and William Still's 'Stove Store'. Other ads in columns 5-7 are repeats.

CR_1865-09-23 p4 (frame 52): poem 'Langley Lane', 'The Kingly Spirit' (from the German), 'How to Get Rich', Miscellaneous Items, then the standing ads (Globe Hotel, Powell, Henderson's, Magarge, African Civilization Society, Army and Navy Intelligence Office, St. Charles United States Hotel, Book Depository catalogue, Gibbons's intelligence office, Longfellow, Johnson and Wear, Duterte, Champion, Charnock, Harding, Avery College, James W. Brown, Brister, Fairhaven boarding, Rodgers). Mrs. H. C. Lunn's Cape Island ad has dropped out. Nothing new.
Mapps: printed 'Miss Grace A. Mapps' and once 'Miss Mapp's place'. 'Fanny Jackson' is Fanny M. Jackson (later Coppin); recorded as printed.
